n: Nahash, king of Ammon (east of the Jordan), dies, and his son Hanun becomes king.

f.w: Nahash the king of the children of Ammon

n: David sends envoys to comfort Hanun, repaying an earlier kindness Nahash had shown him—perhaps during David’s years as a fugitive from Saul.

f.w: his father shewed kindness to me

n: Hanun’s advisers convince him that David’s envoys are spies preparing for an invasion. Suspicion turns kindness into insult.
Hanun humiliates the envoys by shaving them and cutting their robes to expose them. In that culture, this was a deep public insult to David himself.

f.g: 2 Samuel 10:4 specifies half their beards—a grave dishonor for men of that culture.
Right up to their hips, leaving them exposed.

n: David kindly tells the shamed men to stay in Jericho until their beards grow back, sparing them further embarrassment.

f.g: Wait at Jericho, the first town west of the Jordan on their way home.

n: Realizing they have made David their enemy, the Ammonites pay a fortune to hire chariots and soldiers from Aramean kingdoms to the north.

f.g: An enormous sum—roughly 34 tons of silver.

n: The hired forces camp at Medeba, and the Ammonites gather for battle.

f.g: Possibly “chariots and charioteers”; 2 Samuel 10:6 gives the number as foot soldiers.
A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea.

n: David sends Joab with the whole army of seasoned warriors.

f.w: the host of the mighty men
f.g: The army, including David’s elite warriors.

n: The Ammonites line up at their city gate while the Aramean mercenaries take the open field—trapping Israel between two armies.

f.g: Arranged their troops in battle formation.

n: Surrounded front and back, Joab takes the best troops himself to face the Arameans.
He puts his brother Abishai in charge of the rest to face the Ammonites.
The brothers agree to help whichever one is in trouble—a simple picture of teamwork and mutual support.
Joab’s stirring words: be strong and brave for our people and God’s cities, and let the Lord do what seems good to Him. They will do their best and trust God with the outcome.

f.w: let the LORD do that which is good in his sight

n: Joab advances, and the Arameans flee.
Seeing their allies run, the Ammonites retreat into their city. Joab returns to Jerusalem.

f.g: Rabbah, the Ammonite capital (modern Amman, Jordan).

n: The defeated Arameans call for reinforcements from beyond the Euphrates under Shophach, Hadarezer’s commander.
David himself leads all Israel across the Jordan to meet them.
The Arameans are routed, and their commander is killed.

f.w: seven thousand men which fought in chariots
f.g: 2 Samuel 10:18 gives 700 chariots and 40,000 horsemen—differences likely from copying.

n: Hadarezer’s vassals make peace with David and become subject to him. The Arameans refuse to help Ammon again—Hanun’s insult has cost him his allies.
